text:
I read all 10 tracked files. Nothing was run, and nothing was edited. I checked the findings against the policy in `geo.config.json`: AI search crawlers allowed, training crawlers blocked. ## High severity 1. **The pricing page is set to `noindex`.** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` has `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. - The same page has a canonical URL and is listed in `public/sitemap.xml:4`, so the signals contradict each other. - Search engines and AI search will drop your most commercially important page. - Fix: remove the `robots` key. 2. **The blog renders on the client only.** `app/blog/page.tsx:1-10` is a `'use client'` page that fetches `/api/posts` in `useEffect`. - Crawlers, and most AI crawlers that don't run JavaScript, receive an empty `

Blog

`. - The repo has no `/api/posts` route, so the posts may not exist at all. - A client component can't export `metadata`, so the page also has no title or description of its own. - Fix: make it a server component that fetches the posts (or reads them from the filesystem or a CMS) and add `export const metadata`. - Also add per-post routes such as `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`, and list them in the sitemap. Right now individual posts have no URL to be indexed under. ## Medium severity 3. **The `` tag has no `lang`.** `app/layout.tsx:11` should be ``. `geo.config.json:4` already says `en`. 4. **`public/robots.txt` is incomplete.** - Line 5 blocks only `GPTBot`, but the policy blocks all training crawlers. - Fix: add `Disallow: /` groups for `CCBot`, `Google-Extended`, `Applebot-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `Bytespider`, and `Meta-ExternalAgent`. - The `*` group on lines 1-2 already allows the search and retrieval bots (`OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatchatGPT-User`, `PerplexityBot`, `Claude-SearchBot`). Keep it that way and don't add blocks for them. - There is no `Sitemap:` line. Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`. 5. **There is no structured data anywhere.** None of the pages emit JSON-LD. - `app/layout.tsx`: add `Organization` and `WebSite`. - `app/page.tsx`: add `SoftwareApplication`. - `app/pricing/page.tsx`: add `Offer`, plus `FAQPage` if you add FAQs. - `app/docs/page.tsx`: add `TechArticle`. - The blog posts (once they have routes): add `Article`. 6. **The page content is too thin to be cited.** - Home (`app/page.tsx:4`), pricing (`app/pricing/page.tsx:4`) and docs (`app/docs/page.tsx:4`) each have one sentence. - AI answer engines favor pages with concrete facts: what the product does, who it's for, plan limits and prices, setup steps, and a FAQ. - Pricing should state the actual tiers. "Free for up to three people" is the only fact there now. ## Low severity 7. **Page metadata is generic or missing.** - `app/docs/page.tsx:1` has the title "Docs" and no canonical URL. - `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` has the title "Pricing". - `app/blog/page.tsx` has no metadata at all. - Use descriptive titles, for example "Ledger Docs: set up bank feeds" and "Ledger Pricing: free for up to 3 people". - Add `alternates.canonical` to docs and blog. Better, set a default once in `app/layout.tsx:3-7`. 8. **There are no social tags.** `app/layout.tsx:3-7` has no `openGraph` or `twitter` metadata, and there is no share image. 9. **The sitemap has no `lastmod`.** Lines 3-6 of `public/sitemap.xml` list URLs only. Consider generating it with `app/sitemap.ts` so the blog posts are included automatically. 10. **Navigation uses plain `` tags.** `app/layout.tsx:13` should use `next/link` for client-side navigation and prefetching. This is minor for SEO. 11. **Optional: add `/llms.txt`.** It would be a short, curated index of your key pages. Support among AI crawlers is inconsistent, so it's low priority. ## Already correct - `app/thank-you/page.tsx:1` is `noindex` and isn't in the sitemap, which is right. Don't also block it in `robots.txt`, or crawlers won't see the `noindex`. - The canonical URLs and `metadataBase` are consistent with `geo.config.json`. - The `data-nosnippet` on the cookie notice (`app/layout.tsx:15`) is appropriate. If you want, I can apply the fixes. The `noindex` removal, `lang`, `robots.txt` and metadata changes are quick. The blog needs your decision on where the posts come from.
